line.younger: From the first page to the last, God wants to live with his people. Follow the places where he makes his home.
line.older: The whole Bible can be read as one long answer to a question: can God live with his people? Watch where he dwells move from a garden to a tent, a temple, a person, a people, and a whole new world.

key.apart: The closeness is lost, or still waited for

creation.line: God planted a garden and put the people he made there, close to him.

fall.line: The man and the woman hid from God among the trees, and they were sent out of the garden.

abraham.line: God came to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Jacob woke from a dream and said the LORD was in that place.

rescue.line: God went ahead of his people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.

sinai.line: God told Israel to build a tent, the tabernacle, so that he could dwell among them, and his glory filled it.

land.line: In the land, the tent of meeting was set up at Shiloh, among the tribes.

kingdom.line: Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem, and the cloud of God's glory filled it.

exile.line: The prophet Ezekiel saw God's glory leave the temple before Babylon destroyed it.

return.line: The people rebuilt the temple, and God promised that one day he would fill it with glory.

jesus.line: Jesus is God with us. The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us.

cross.line: When Jesus died, the curtain that closed off the most holy place in the temple tore from top to bottom.

church.line: God's Spirit came to live in his people. Paul tells the church that it is now God's temple.

new-creation.line: At the end, God's dwelling place is with people, and he lives with them for ever.

line.younger: God makes promises to his people, and he always keeps them.
line.older: God binds himself to people by covenant: with Noah, Abraham, Israel at Sinai and David, and at last the new covenant in Jesus.

line.younger: Again and again a lamb dies in the place of someone else, until Jesus, the Lamb of God.
line.older: Sacrifice runs from the garden to the cross: a substitute, a covering, a price paid by another.

line.younger: God's people wait for a good king, and Jesus is that king.
line.older: People made to rule under God want to rule without him. The story looks for the true king, the son of David, who reigns by serving.

line.younger: God's plan was always for people from every country.
line.older: Through Abraham's family God means to bless all the families of the earth, and the last pages show people from every nation together.
